onboarding.title: Set up TankLog in minutes
onboarding.subtitle: Create a Supabase project, apply the schema, paste keys, then create your account.
onboarding.step1a: Open supabase.com and create a free project.
onboarding.step1c: Recommended: Data API ON, auto-expose tables OFF, automatic RLS ON.
onboarding.step3Body: From Project Settings → API: Project URL and anon public key. Never use the service_role key.
onboarding.schemaStillMissing: Schema not detected yet — finish the SQL step, then recheck.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.subtitle: TankLog is a static app. Your aquarium data lives in the Supabase project you control.
privacy.byoBody: TankLog does not host a shared multi-tenant database. Auth, Postgres rows, and photo files stay in your project. The static site only talks to the URL and anon key you paste locally.
privacy.localBody: Supabase URL, anon key, language preference, active tank id, optional OneSignal App ID / proxy settings, and (optionally) a temporary Google Client ID for migration are stored in localStorage on this browser. Sessions use Supabase auth storage for that project.
privacy.googleBody: Daily use does not require Google. The migration wizard may ask for a temporary OAuth Client ID and read-only Drive/Sheets access to import v1 data once. Disconnect clears that Client ID from the device.
privacy.oneSignalBody: Background web push is optional and BYO: you create the OneSignal app. The App ID and proxy URL stay in localStorage. The OneSignal REST API key must live only in your scheduling proxy (e.g. Cloudflare Worker), never in the browser.
privacy.controlBody: You can export JSON from Settings, disconnect the project (clears local keys), delete data in your Supabase dashboard, or stop using the static site at any time.
